lessons.title: ForgeDesk ticket 8801 — git conflict on the deploy branch
lessons.markdown:
# Week 1: ForgeDesk ticket 8801 — git conflict on the deploy branch

The WAIKE Software ForgeDesk is a two-person civic issue tracker for Device Lab checkouts. Ticket 8801 opens when a volunteer edits routes.py on feature/kiosk-hours while the desk lead edited the same function on main. A conflict is not a personality crisis. It is two hashes that claim the same lines. You will read both sides, keep the authz guard that main added, and keep the hours table that the feature branch added.

Branch names in this course are contracts. main is always deployable to the local Device Lab compose stack. Feature branches must merge with an explicit conflict report JSON that names the surviving function signature. The lab rejects a resolution that drops require_role or that keeps both copies as _v1 and _v2 without a test.

CS50 Web Git week is a structure citation only. Harvard lab text stays at Harvard. WAIKE conflict fixture is original: two parents, one file, one required survivor set. Publicly viewable is not free to copy. AI mode for practice drills: PRACTICE; for the graded conflict report: AI_DISCLOSED if you used HINT.

## Concept and boundary

Version control records changes, not correctness. A commit identifies a project state; a branch names a movable line of development. A merge conflict means Git could not choose an edit automatically. Deleting conflict markers without understanding both changes can silently discard behavior.

## Guided implementation

Create a new local practice repository containing a two-line runbook. Commit it. Make two branches that edit the same line differently, commit on each, then merge one into the other. Expected result: Git identifies the conflicting path. Read both edits, write a combined version that preserves the intended requirements, stage it, and commit. Confirm with `git status` and inspect the final file. If you cannot explain the conflict, stop; preserve both branches instead of resetting away their work.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Document both original requirements, the final decision and a test that would detect a lost requirement. Repeat with edits to separate lines and explain why a conflict may not occur. Use only a disposable local repository; do not practice force-pushing on a shared branch.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## First-programming bridge

If variables, functions or tests are new, open **Your first program** in the reader’s downloadable worked examples before attempting the infrastructure lab. Save `capacity.py` and `test_capacity.py` with its README in one folder. The guide teaches assignment versus comparison, numeric types, branches, return values, exceptions and boundary tests through the Digital Confidence capacity case. It includes a separate workload-planning challenge with a reviewer rubric. A checked fixture does not establish independent programming competence. Return here to specify a requirement and observable acceptance criteria for your own function.

## Worked example

Parents A and B both touch def open_hours. A adds require_role('desk'). B adds HOURS={...}. Survivor must include both tokens.

lessons.title: REST for checkout — status codes that mean something
lessons.markdown:
# Week 2: REST for checkout — status codes that mean something

ForgeDesk exposes /api/v1/checkouts. GET inventing a device returns 404 with a stable error body, not 200 with null. POST without device_id returns 400. POST from reader role against a write route returns 403. Successful POST returns 201 and Location /api/v1/checkouts/{id}.

You will build a route table in JSON and prove each case. The lab computes expected status from method, path, role, and body keys. Idempotent PUT on the same checkout id must not mint a second row.

Secure-development practice: validate input before storage, return problem-style errors without stack traces, never echo secrets. GitHub Actions will later call these routes in CI against an in-memory store.

Status codes are evidence. Inventing a device_id must yield 404 with a problem body that names the missing resource, never a 200 with null. A reader POST to a write route yields 403; a desk POST without device_id yields 400; a successful desk POST yields 201 plus Location /api/v1/checkouts/{id}. The lab recomputes expected status from method, path, role, and body keys — a screenshot of Postman is not acceptance. Idempotent PUT on the same checkout id must not mint a second row. Secure-dev habit: validate before storage, never echo secrets, keep error bodies stable for CI asserts.

## Concept and boundary

A request contract defines allowed inputs, state transitions and observable results. HTTP status families communicate classes of outcomes; application semantics determine which success or error status is appropriate. A successful read must not silently perform a checkout.

## Guided implementation

Run the downloadable checkout worked example. Predict GET for demo-1, POST by reader, POST by desk, then a second POST by desk. Expected results in this fixture: available, forbidden, checkout created, conflict. These are local function results modeling an API contract; no HTTP server or physical checkout occurs. Inspect the role and state checks in that order.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Add another fictional item and demonstrate that mutation is isolated to the requested item. State what a real HTTP adapter would need for validated input, authenticated identity and error handling.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

POST as reader with device_id → 403. POST as desk missing device_id → 400. GET missing → 404. Create → 201.

lessons.title: Migrations that do not strand the Device Lab
lessons.markdown:
# Week 3: Migrations that do not strand the Device Lab

Checkout rows live in SQLite for local Device Lab and Postgres in staging. Week 3 is migration discipline. Migration 0003_add_returned_at must add a nullable timestamp, bump schema_version to 3, and leave a down migration that drops the column without deleting checkout history.

A migration that hard-codes production passwords fails. A migration that DELETE FROM checkouts to make room fails. CS50 Web SQL/models week is a domain label only. Fixture SQL is original WAIKE wording for ForgeDesk.

Assessment mode AI_RESTRICTED for the SQL artifact: you may use EXPLAIN orally with an instructor, but the submitted forward/down SQL must be authored without generative paste.

Migration 0003_add_returned_at adds a nullable timestamp, bumps schema_version to 3, and ships a down migration that drops only that column. Hard-coding production passwords, DELETE FROM checkouts to free space, or skipping the down migration fails. Local Device Lab uses SQLite; staging uses Postgres — your SQL must stay dialect-honest for the fixture dialect the lab names. Assessment mode AI_RESTRICTED: EXPLAIN orally with an instructor is fine; the submitted forward/down SQL is authored without generative paste. CS50 Web models week is a domain label only.

## Concept and boundary

A database schema defines stored structure and constraints. A migration changes that schema or data representation between versions. A transaction groups operations so they succeed or fail together within the database guarantees. Backup and tested rollback address different risks from a successful schema command.

## Guided implementation

Inspect the example CREATE TABLE statement. Explain the primary key and the constraint allowing only 0 or 1. In a disposable copy, try inserting a duplicate ID and an invalid availability value; Expected result: both invalid inserts fail their constraints. Catch errors explicitly when experimenting, then verify the original row remains readable. Do not run exploratory migrations on a shared database.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Design a migration adding an optional shelf label. Specify the before/after schema, treatment of existing rows, validation query and recovery procedure. Explain which changes can be reversed without information loss and which need a backup. This design is not evidence of a performed production migration.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

Forward adds returned_at TIMESTAMP NULL; schema_version=3; down drops returned_at only.

lessons.title: Frontend contract — accessible checkout board
lessons.markdown:
# Week 4: Frontend contract — accessible checkout board

The ForgeDesk board is a single HTML page with a table of checkouts. Accessibility is not a slide. Every overdue signal needs text marker OVERDUE, not color alone. The filter must be a button named Filter overdue. API failures render in a role=alert region.

The lab parses a DOM-like JSON tree. Broken API JSON must not fail silently. This is original WAIKE UI work, not a CS50 project port.

AI mode COMPARE_APPROACHES allowed when weighing table vs card layouts; disclose the comparison in the assignment footer.

Every overdue row shows a text marker OVERDUE, not color alone. The filter control is a button named exactly Filter overdue. API failures render inside a role=alert region; broken JSON must not blank the board. The lab parses a DOM-like JSON tree and checks those contracts. COMPARE_APPROACHES is allowed when weighing table versus card layouts if you disclose the comparison in the assignment footer. This is original ForgeDesk UI work, not a port of any CS50 frontend project.

## Concept and boundary

An interface has a visual presentation and an interaction contract. Labels connect controls to their purpose. Keyboard focus identifies the active control. Color alone should not carry the only explanation of an error or status. A button click is not proof that the server accepted a mutation.

## Guided implementation

Sketch an accessible checkout form with an item label, submit button, pending state, success state and error state. Write text for a 403 denial and a 409 state conflict. Expected result: the user can distinguish missing permission from an already checked-out item without relying on color. If you implement it, test the entire path using only the keyboard and preserve focus after validation failure.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Create a test plan covering a duplicate submission, a network failure and a long item name. For each, state the expected visible feedback and whether the original input is retained. Record actual observations separately from planned outcomes.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

Tree includes button Filter overdue, table, OVERDUE text for ring-7, and role=alert.

lessons.title: Authz matrix — desk vs reader vs forge-bot
lessons.markdown:
# Week 5: Authz matrix — desk vs reader vs forge-bot

Roles: desk can create and close checkouts. reader can GET only. forge-bot can annotate but cannot close. The lab evaluates an action matrix. Granting forge-bot checkout.close is the package negative.

AI-use mode REVIEW_MY_WORK: assistants may critique your matrix; the submitted JSON is yours and AI assistance must be disclosed (AI_DISCLOSED).

Distinct vocabulary from Harbor SOC avoids noun-swapped templates across batches.

desk may create and close checkouts; reader may GET only; forge-bot may annotate but never close. The lab evaluates an action matrix against those rules. Granting forge-bot checkout.close is the package negative and must fail. REVIEW_MY_WORK assistants may critique your matrix; the submitted JSON is yours and must carry AI_DISCLOSED when used. Keep vocabulary distinct from Harbor SOC so batch-001 and batch-002 authz labs are not noun-swapped clones.

## Concept and boundary

Authorization must be checked where the protected action is performed. Hiding a UI control is not enforcement. A caller-supplied role is untrusted unless an authenticated, authorized system established it. The local example uses role strings solely to make the policy visible.

## Guided implementation

Read the reader denial test, run it, then temporarily remove the POST authorization check in your disposable copy. Expected result: the denial test fails. Restore the check and rerun. Explain why the test distinguishes an enforced policy from an interface convention. No real accounts are created.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Draw an access matrix for reader, desk and automation roles. Add a test for an unknown role. Explain how an actual server would resolve identity from its established session rather than accepting a JSON field as proof of authority.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

desk:{create,close,read}; reader:{read}; forge-bot:{annotate}. Bot close fails.

# Week 6: Automated tests that catch the silent 200

Parse a JUnit-like JSON report: total, failed, skipped. Acceptance requires failed==0, total>=8, and a named test test_reader_post_forbidden with status passed. A green badge PNG is not evidence. Aligns to CS50 Web testing themes and secure-dev prove-the-negative-path without copying those item banks. NO_AI applies to the practical portion of any quiz makeup that reuses this week's fixture.

Journal week 6 (Automated tests that catch the silent 200): keep the artifact id, fixture counts, and computed fields; adjectives are not evidence.

Acceptance for week 6 still names ticket-linked digests, HTTP status fields, schema_version, DOM contracts, role actions, JUnit counts, workflow gates, digests, severity bands, or error-budget arithmetic the next shift can reopen without tribal knowledge.

Acceptance for week 6 still names ticket-linked digests, HTTP status fields, schema_version, DOM contracts, role actions, JUnit counts, workflow gates, digests, severity bands, or error-budget arithmetic the next shift can reopen without tribal knowledge.

## Concept and boundary

A test compares an observation with an expected result. A passing test supports only the cases and assertions it exercises. Tests can be wrong or incomplete. A negative test deliberately checks that an invalid action is rejected without changing protected state.

## Guided implementation

Read all six worked-example tests. For each assertion, name the requirement it checks. Change the expected conflict status to 200 and run the suite; the deliberate failure confirms that the assertion is being executed. Restore it. Next remove the authorization condition and observe a different failure. Expected result: both controlled defects are detected.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Add tests for unsupported methods and unrecognized roles. Include an assertion on stored state after rejection. Explain one behavior your tests still do not establish, such as concurrent requests, network delivery or recovery after a disk failure.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

Report total=10 failed=0 skipped=1 includes test_reader_post_forbidden passed=true.

lessons.title: GitHub Actions — CI that blocks bad merges
lessons.markdown:
# Week 7: GitHub Actions — CI that blocks bad merges

Workflow forge-ci must run on pull_request, lint, test, and upload the report artifact. Lab validates workflow JSON: triggers, ordered jobs, and deploy not on PR without environment gate. Echo PASS fails.

GitHub Actions docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY. We write our own workflow model. AI mode DEBUG_WITH_ME allowed on red workflows with disclosure.

Compose and CI logs for week 7 are evidence; adjectives are not. Keep digest and status fields typed.

Workflow forge-ci runs on pull_request, runs lint then test, and uploads the report artifact. Deploy must not run on PR without an environment gate. The lab validates triggers, ordered jobs, and that gate. Echoing PASS as the job script fails the print-PASS ban. GitHub Actions docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY; write ForgeDesk's own workflow model. DEBUG_WITH_ME is allowed on red workflows with disclosure.

## Concept and boundary

Continuous integration runs configured checks against a particular source revision. It does not by itself prevent merges: repository protection must require the relevant checks. Passing tests do not establish that dependencies, secrets handling or deployment permissions are safe.

## Guided implementation

Write a CI job that checks out the source, selects a documented Python version and runs the example tests from their directory. Rehearse that command locally in a fresh folder containing only the two downloaded files. Expected result: the same six tests pass without a hidden local dependency. Keep credentials out of the workflow.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Introduce the same controlled authorization defect and show that the CI test command exits unsuccessfully. Document the exact commit and command. If no authorized CI service is available, label the result a local rehearsal rather than a remote CI run.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

on:[pull_request]; jobs lint → test → upload-report; no ungated deploy on PR.

lessons.title: Deploy and rollback on Device Lab compose
lessons.markdown:
# Week 8: Deploy and rollback on Device Lab compose

Deploy pins image digest sha256:… to local compose and writes rollback pointer to previous digest. Lab checks rollback_to != current and health healthy only after migrate=ok. Skipping migrate fails.

Physical flashing out of scope; Device Lab here is digital compose. Capstone preview: issue through deploy artifact path.

Compose and CI logs for week 8 are evidence; adjectives are not. Keep digest and status fields typed.

Deploy pins image digest sha256:… into local compose and writes rollback_to to the previous digest. Health may read healthy only after migrate=ok. Skipping migrate, leaving rollback_to equal to current, or claiming a physical flash for this digital compose target fails. Capstone preview: follow one issue fixture through branch, CI, migrate, deploy. PHYSICAL flashing stays out of scope for Software Builder.

Journal week 8 (Deploy and rollback on Device Lab compose): keep the artifact id, fixture counts, and computed fields; adjectives are not evidence.

## Concept and boundary

Deployment moves a specific build into an environment. Rollback selects or restores a previously usable state, but an older application may be incompatible with a newer database. A version label without an immutable artifact or source identifier is insufficient for reproduction.

## Guided implementation

Prepare two disposable folders with known source revisions and a manifest recording their hashes. Rehearse switching a local test command between them. Expected result: you can identify which version was tested and reproduce its result. Simulate a failed check, then select the earlier version and repeat the check. No production service is affected.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Write a release gate that includes tests, schema compatibility, authorization, observability and a rollback trigger. Specify who has authority to release. A paper runbook is a design artifact, not proof that a live deployment or rollback succeeded.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

current=sha256:aaa rollback_to=sha256:bbb migrate=ok health=healthy.

# Week 9: Security review — findings with severity bands

Review ForgeDesk for IDOR on checkout ids, missing login rate limit, verbose 500s. Lab scores findings: id, severity band, evidence. At least one high/critical for intentional IDOR fixture. Empty 'looks fine' fails.

OWASP ASVS themes are domain labels — no copied item banks. Practical assessment mode: NO_AI.

Compose and CI logs for week 9 are evidence; adjectives are not. Keep digest and status fields typed.

Score findings with id, severity band, and evidence. At least one high or critical must name the intentional IDOR fixture on checkout ids. Empty looks-fine reviews fail. Also watch missing login rate limits and verbose 500s that leak stack traces. OWASP ASVS themes are domain labels — no copied item banks. Practical assessment mode: NO_AI.

Journal week 9 (Security review — findings with severity bands): keep the artifact id, fixture counts, and computed fields; adjectives are not evidence.

## Concept and boundary

A security finding connects an observed weakness to a possible impact, affected scope, evidence and remediation. Severity depends on context; a tool label alone does not establish exploitability. Review within a defined authorization boundary and avoid real personal data.

## Guided implementation

Inspect the worked example for its explicit trust limits. Identify parameter-bound SQL as one defense against treating item IDs as executable SQL, and caller-supplied role strings as a reason the fixture cannot serve as real authentication. Run the quotation-containing input test. Expected result: the input is treated as a missing ID, not as a query that returns all rows.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Write two findings: one about using the role argument in a real service without authentication, and one about missing operational controls. Include evidence, limits, a proposed fix and a retest. Do not turn the exercise into scanning or exploitation of another system.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

Findings include FORGE-IDOR-1 severity=high with evidence lacking owner check.

lessons.markdown:
# Week 10: Observability and issue→deploy capstone

SLO: checkout API availability 99.5% over fixture window. Compute error budget from failed/total. Capstone: real ForgeDesk issue fixture through branch, CI, migrate, deploy, observability note. No fabricated community impact numbers.

Career map: junior software builder / Device Lab integrator. Certs aligned not granted. Academic: CS50/CS50 Web structure citations only.

AI modes used across the course must appear in the capstone disclosure table: EXPLAIN/HINT/QUESTION_ME/DEBUG_WITH_ME/REVIEW_MY_WORK/COMPARE_APPROACHES/PRACTICE mapped to assessment modes AI_ALLOWED / AI_RESTRICTED / AI_DISCLOSED / NO_AI.

SLO availability is 99.5% over the fixture window. Error budget = 1 − availability from failed/total counts the lab recomputes. Capstone ships a real ForgeDesk issue fixture through branch, CI, migrate, deploy, and an observability note — no fabricated community impact numbers. Career map: junior software builder / Device Lab integrator; certs aligned not granted. Capstone disclosure table must map EXPLAIN/HINT/QUESTION_ME/DEBUG_WITH_ME/REVIEW_MY_WORK/COMPARE_APPROACHES/PRACTICE to AI_ALLOWED / AI_RESTRICTED / AI_DISCLOSED / NO_AI.

## Concept and boundary

Observability connects external outcomes to internal events without exposing unnecessary information. Counts, timings and logs answer different questions. A log that merely exists is not evidence that the application met the user need or that an incident was resolved.

## Guided implementation

Run one allowed checkout, one repeated checkout and one denied checkout in a fresh fixture. Inspect its event list. Expected result: status and outcome are recorded, while no patron name, password or item text is logged. Count the outcomes and explain which request sequence produced them. Distinguish the fictional event trace from real service telemetry.

## Independent evidence and recovery

Assemble the capstone: issue description, requirement-to-test map, exact source version, test output including a controlled failure, authorization matrix, migration plan, release/rollback rehearsal and redacted findings. A reviewer must rerun the example and inspect your independent tests. Record completion as pending until actual practical evidence and authorized review meet the course criteria.

If a result differs, preserve the failing output and the exact file revision. Change one assumption at a time, rerun the relevant check, and explain what the new evidence supports. Do not mark an unperformed step complete.

## Worked example

failed=50 total=10000 → availability=0.995; budget_ok true.

# Software Builder — ForgeDesk to Device Lab Deploy

## Who this is for
Ten weeks on ForgeDesk: git conflict, REST, migrations, accessible UI, authz, tests, GitHub Actions, deploy/rollback, security review, observability. Capstone is issue→deployed local/Device-Lab artifact. CS50/CS50 Web and Actions docs are structure citations only. No dumps.

## Tracks and academy
- Tracks: SOFTWARE_BUILDER
- Academy: ACADEMY_SOFTWARE

## Duration
Ten ForgeDesk weeks (~8–10 hours/week including CI red-build time). Not a two-hour HTML workshop. Device Lab compose is scheduled; do not deploy ungated on pull_request.

## Weekly map
- Week 01: ForgeDesk ticket 8801 — git conflict on the deploy branch
- Week 02: REST for checkout — status codes that mean something
- Week 03: Migrations that do not strand the Device Lab
- Week 04: Frontend contract — accessible checkout board
- Week 05: Authz matrix — desk vs reader vs forge-bot
- Week 06: Automated tests that catch the silent 200
- Week 07: GitHub Actions — CI that blocks bad merges
- Week 08: Deploy and rollback on Device Lab compose
- Week 09: Security review — findings with severity bands
- Week 10: Observability and issue→deploy capstone

## Assessments
ForgeDesk assessment mix: weekly builder quizzes on ticket 8801-class numbers, a mid-course audit (20 original items on conflict/REST/migrate/authz/CI), a final (24 original items on deploy/security/SLO/capstone path), a practical over ten runnable labs that reject empty/wrong/print-PASS, and an issue-to-deploy group project. Silent 200 on forbidden writes scores zero.

## Claim boundary
Aligns to CS50/CS50 Web topic shape and GitHub Actions docs as PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY. Secure-dev themes are labels. Does not grant vendor certs. Instructor keys stay out of the learner packet.

Merge a real conflict, ship a checkout API, and pin a digest on local Device Lab compose.

# Checkout contract worked example

New to programming? Start with the downloadable **Your first program** guide and its `capacity.py` / `test_capacity.py` files, then return here.

Prerequisites: Python 3.11+ on a computer you control, a text editor and ability to open a terminal in a folder. Uses Python's standard library only. No network service, packages, accounts or real library data are needed.

Download `checkout.py` and `test_checkout.py` into the same empty folder. From that folder run:

```
python3 -m unittest -v test_checkout.py
```

On Windows where the Python launcher is installed, use `py -3 -m unittest -v test_checkout.py`. Expected result: six tests pass. A missing Python command means the runtime prerequisite is unmet; do not copy commands from an unknown download site. A module import error usually means you ran from the wrong folder or did not save both files with `.py` extensions.

Read each assertion and predict its result before running. Then deliberately change the reader authorization check to allow POST, rerun and observe the failed denial test. Restore the original condition and rerun. Save the before/after result; a screenshot of a green test run alone does not show that you understand why it passed.

Independent work: add a second fictional item and tests showing that checking out the first does not change the second. Add a test for an unsupported method and a separate test for an unrecognized role. Explain why a user-supplied role string would be unsafe in a real web service. Do not use this exercise as an authentication or production database implementation.

This is a local worked example, not execution of the canonical ForgeDesk infrastructure labs. Those require their documented artifact schemas and authorized environment. AI assistance contributed to the example and tests. Human technical and educational acceptance remains pending. resources.markdown:
# Your first program: turn a capacity question into a tested function

Start here before the Checkout contract example if variables, functions or automated tests are unfamiliar. You need the Digital Confidence file-saving and capacity activities, a plain-text editor, and Python 3.11 or later installed on a computer you control. No administrator privileges, packages, web account or network are required. If the runtime is unavailable, use your authorized teaching environment; do not install a random executable to bypass that prerequisite.

By the end you should be able to explain the difference between text and numbers, call a function with different inputs, predict a branch, diagnose a failed test and revise your own code. Passing these example tests is practice; it is not independent evidence of those skills.

## 1. Save and run a program

Download `capacity.py` and `test_capacity.py` together into a new folder you own. Show filename extensions in your file manager if necessary; `capacity.py.txt` is a text document with the wrong name for these commands. Open a terminal in that folder. A terminal accepts commands as text; its current folder determines where relative filenames are found. Run:

```
python3 --version
python3 capacity.py
```

Where the Windows Python launcher is already installed, use `py -3` in place of `python3`. The first command identifies the interpreter, which reads and runs Python code. The second names a file to run; typing the filename into an editor does not execute it. Expected output is:

```
Usable free: 25.000%; meets fixture policy
```

The program uses fictional storage values. It does not inspect or modify your real disk. Do not paste your home-directory name or other personal information into evidence.

## 2. Read one statement at a time

A variable gives a value a name. In `total = 256`, `=` assigns a value; it is different from `==`, which compares values. The integer `256` supports arithmetic. The text `"256"` is a string; it must be validated and converted before arithmetic. This example deliberately accepts only whole-number GiB inputs, so it rejects strings, fractional measurements and booleans rather than silently guessing what they mean.

`def capacity(total, used, reserve):` defines a reusable function. Indented lines are its body. Parameters are local names receiving the caller's inputs. `capacity(256, 180, 12)` calls that function with three arguments. Parentheses group the subtraction before division: `(256 - 180 - 12) / 256 * 100` is 25.0. All three values must use the same unit. The reserve is separate from used capacity in this fixture; subtracting a reserve already included in used would be a different model.

`if free_percent >= 15:` selects a branch. The threshold is a teaching policy, not a universal operating-system requirement. A below-policy result can be an accurate answer. `return` sends a result back to the caller. The returned dictionary has named entries, accessed as `result['free_percent']`; it is not a database and is not saved after the process exits.

Before changing any code, predict `capacity(256, 220, 12)`. The remaining 24 GiB is 9.375%, so the policy branch should say `below`. Change only the example call at the bottom, save, rerun and compare. Restore the original call afterward. If the output stays unchanged, confirm that you saved the same file that the terminal runs.

## 3. Reject impossible inputs before computing

A total of zero cannot be a divisor. Negative capacity and used-plus-reserve exceeding total are invalid for this fixture. The function raises `ValueError` for these cases. An exception stops the normal return path and describes why the input was rejected. We do not catch every exception and print a success message: rejection is part of the contract.

Try a deliberate error in the example call: `capacity(0, 0, 0)`. Read the final exception line, then locate the filename and line number above it. Expected result: `ValueError: total must be positive`. Restore the valid call. Keep the error and repaired output in your fictional practice journal. A traceback is diagnostic evidence; it does not mean the computer has been damaged.

## 4. Read and run an automated test

Run:

```
python3 -m unittest -v test_capacity.py
```

`-m unittest` asks Python to run its standard test tool. It imports the named test file. Importing `capacity.py` defines its function, but the `if __name__ == '__main__':` guard keeps the demonstration print from running during import. Expected result: nine tests pass, including invalid inputs. Each assertion compares observed behavior with an independently specified expectation. A green run only covers these cases.

In `test_exact_threshold`, a 200 GiB volume with 160 used and 10 reserved leaves 30 GiB, exactly 15%. The test expects `meets`. Temporarily change the function's comparison from `>=` to `>` and run the suite. That boundary test must fail. Read expected versus actual, restore `>=`, and run again. Do not change the test to hide the failure.

Troubleshooting: `ModuleNotFoundError` usually means one file is missing, renamed or in another folder. `SyntaxError` often means an unmatched quote, bracket or colon. `IndentationError` means the block indentation is inconsistent; compare the reference's spaces. A failed assertion means the code ran but differed from the expected behavior. Check the named case before editing unrelated lines. Work in a copy if you need to preserve the original.

## 5. Independent variation and review

Create a separate `capacity_plan.py`. Write a function taking total, used, separate reserve and a proposed **additional** workload in whole GiB. It must report free percentage after the workload, whether the workload physically fits, and whether the resulting state meets the same 15% policy. Define what happens when it does not fit; do not return an ordinary successful capacity result for an impossible state. Keep physically fitting and policy-compliant as separate concepts.

Choose your own fictional inputs. Include a fitting case above policy, a fitting case below policy, an exactly-at-policy case, a workload that exceeds free capacity, zero total, a negative workload, and a text input. Calculate expected results before running your code. Write tests for each and demonstrate one deliberate defect that a test catches. No reference solution for this independent variation is included here.

Deliver your source, tests, expected-results table, before/failure/repair output and a short explanation of one limitation. Explain the branches in your own words. A reviewer checks arithmetic, validation, the distinct fit/policy decisions, meaningful tests and your revision process. They may ask for changed inputs or a live explanation. Revision is expected when a criterion is unmet; submission alone does not award mastery. If you used AI or other help, identify what it supplied and what you independently checked.

Return to Software Builder Week 1 to connect a plain-language requirement to this function's contract. Continue to the Checkout contract worked example once you can explain the parameter, return value, branch and boundary test without reading a script. Git, HTTP and SQLite will introduce additional concepts; this local program does not implement those systems.

AI assistance contributed to this guide, code and tests. Human technical and educational acceptance is pending. Repository software licensing applies; no third-party assets or real learner data are included.
